cases.title: An agent asks before a risky action
cases.situation: The agent is about to do something that changes shared work or is hard to undo.
cases.answer: An action is risky when it changes shared work or is hard to undo. In a product that works with code, that includes opening or merging a pull request, deleting files, closing an issue and rolling back a release. Carrying out a plan of several changes is risky too. Before a risky action the agent stops and posts a card with the exact action: every step it will take, or the changes themselves, which the person can open. The agent does nothing until the person presses the approve button.
cases.why: A person can only approve what they can see, and an agent's mistake in shared work costs other people.
do: List every step in the card, in the order the agent will do them.
Offer a way to see the full changes, such as a View Changes button, before the approve button is pressed.
Let the person edit the plan or cancel it, not only approve it.
Once decided, mark the card Approved or Cancelled and remove its buttons.
dont: Do not carry out a risky action before the person approves it.
Do not replace the steps or the changes with a one-line summary.
Do not let the agent write the label of an approve or merge button.
Do not let a second click on a decided card approve or cancel it again.
cases.notBuiltYet: In Scindo the agent asks before carrying out a plan, opening a pull request and merging one. It does not yet ask before deleting files, closing an issue or rolling back a release.

cases.title: An agent cancels and reports when nobody answers
cases.situation: The agent has asked a question or proposed an action, and nobody answers.
cases.answer: The agent never takes silence as a yes: while a question or proposal waits, it does nothing that depends on the answer. Each product sets the waiting time and shows it on the waiting card. When the time is up, the agent cancels the request, marks the card Cancelled, and posts one line saying what it did not do. The agent may write a plan that lists the unanswered questions as open questions. It may not carry out anything that depends on an answer.
cases.why: An agent that acts on silence does work nobody approved, and one that waits forever leaves work stuck without saying so.
do: Keep the card and its buttons open until someone answers or the request is cancelled.
Notify the person who asked when the agent needs their answer.
When a request is cancelled, mark the card Cancelled and post one line on what was not done.
List questions asked before a plan that nobody answered as open questions in that plan.
dont: Do not treat no answer as approval.
Do not cancel a request without saying so in the thread.
cases.notBuiltYet: No product cancels a waiting request on its own yet. In Scindo a request waits until a person answers, cancels or skips it, and the waiting time is not decided.

cases.title: An agent refuses clearly
cases.situation: The product will not let the agent answer a request, for example because the workspace used all its agent replies for the month, reached its spending cap, or sent too many requests at once.
cases.answer: The refusal says in one plain sentence which limit was reached, and either who can change it or when to try again. A person who can lift the limit gets the one button that does it, such as Upgrade or Change Budget Cap. When an admin can lift the limit, everyone else is told to ask a workspace admin. A limit that passes with time says when to try again instead.
cases.why: A person who is refused needs to know why and what to do next, or they will just send the request again.
do: Say which limit was reached, with the number when there is one: 'You've used all 50 AI agent responses this month.'
Say who can change it, or when to try again: 'Try again in a minute.'
Show the button that lifts the limit only to a person allowed to use it.
Let the person close the refusal without acting, with a button such as 'Not Now'.
dont: Do not show a general error message for a refusal.
Do not show an Upgrade button to someone who cannot upgrade.
cases.native: On Apple the refusal is a row above the composer, with an Upgrade or Change Budget Cap button for admins and never a link to a web page.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web does not follow this yet: it shows the Upgrade button to everyone. Scindo's Apple app shows it only to admins.

cases.title: An agent says what it is
cases.situation: The agent posts in a thread where people also write, or replies to a person.
cases.answer: Every agent message has marks no person's message has. It shows an icon avatar instead of a photo, and the agent's own name. When the product knows which model wrote the reply, it shows the model name in small text next to the time. An agent the workspace connects from outside gets a plain bot icon, not the product's logo.
cases.why: People must see at a glance whether a person or an agent wrote what they are reading, and whose agent it is.
do: Show the agent with an icon avatar, never a photo or an initial.
Name the agent in the message header: its role or given name, or 'Agent' when it has none.
Show the model name next to the time when the product knows it.
Show the product's logo on the product's own agent and a plain bot icon on an agent from outside, so people see whose agent it is.
dont: Do not show a photo for an agent, even when one is set.
Do not show the product's logo on an agent the product does not run.
cases.native: On Apple an 'Agent' label with a sparkles icon sits next to a named agent's name, and the app draws the agent's avatar itself.

cases.title: An agent shows its progress
cases.situation: The agent is working on a request and its reply is not ready yet.
cases.answer: While it works, the agent shows a live row in the thread, where its reply will appear: its name, the model, the seconds so far, the steps it has finished with a check mark, and the step it is on now in plain words, such as 'Reading file'. A Stop button stays on that row for the whole run. When the run is stopped, the agent posts a short note that it stopped.
cases.why: A person waiting on an agent needs to know it is still working, what it is doing, and that they can stop it.
do: Show the progress row in the thread, where the reply will appear.
Name the current step in plain words, such as 'Reading file' or 'Editing code'.
Keep finished steps in view, each with a check mark.
Keep a Stop button on the row for the whole run.
dont: Do not show a spinner with no words.
Do not hide the Stop button while the agent writes its reply.
Do not say the agent stopped before the run has really ended.
cases.native: On Apple the Send button turns into Stop while the agent works, and the note reads 'Stopped.' only once the run has really ended.

cases.title: An agent shows its sources
cases.situation: The agent answers from things it read: documents, files, chat, tasks, or a connected service such as a code host or a design tool.
cases.answer: Under the reply, the agent lists what it used. A small tag names the kinds of source, such as 'From Chat · Knowledge base', and one card per source shows its title, its kind and where it lives. Each card opens the source. A reply that used no sources shows no sources section.
cases.why: A person can check an answer only when they can open what it came from.
do: Put the sources directly under the reply they support.
Show each source as a card with its title and where it lives, such as the space name or the date.
Make each card open the source itself, in the product or on the service it came from.
Show the first six sources and a 'Show N more' button for the rest.
dont: Do not show a sources section when the reply used no sources.
Do not show source cards on a person's message.
Do not link a source card to any site other than the product or the service the source came from.

cases.title: Confirm a destructive action
cases.situation: A person asks to delete or remove something, and it cannot be undone.
do: Follow the rule 'Confirm dialogs' for the Modal: `size="small"`, 'Cancel' first, then the action with `color="danger"`.
Name the thing and what goes with it: "This deletes 'Q3 plan' and its 12 tasks."
Turn the row's Buttons into 'Cancel' and a danger 'Remove' in place for the inline confirm. The rest of the row stays as it is.
Give each row's Buttons an `aria-label` that names the thing, such as 'Remove Dana Lee', 'Cancel removing Dana Lee' and 'Confirm removing Dana Lee', so a screen reader knows which row they act on.
Keep one row confirming at a time. Starting a confirm on another row cancels the first.
Show a toast that names the thing once it is gone.
dont: Do not ask for a confirm when the action is easy to undo.
Do not remove a row on the first click of its Button.
Do not open a Modal for a row in a long list when the inline confirm keeps the place.
Do not ask a question in place of the action, such as 'Are you sure?'.
cases.native: On Apple use a system `confirmationDialog` or `.alert`, with the action in the `.destructive` role and 'Cancel' in the `.cancel` role.
cases.notBuiltYet: Commentify's Delete project confirm is not danger-colored and asks a question in its body. Scindo on the web confirms removing a saved card in place, but asks 'Are you sure?' and labels its Buttons 'Confirm' and 'No'.

options.title: Confirm in a Modal
options.useWhen: The default, for any delete or remove that cannot be undone.

options.title: Confirm in the row
options.useWhen: The action is on a row inside a dense list, and a Modal would lose the place.

cases.title: Confirm dialogs
cases.situation: An action a person takes themselves needs their yes before it happens. An action the agent wants to take follows the rule 'An agent asks before a risky action', a card in the conversation, not this one.
cases.answer: A confirm is a Modal with `size="small"`. Its title names the action in Title Case, such as 'Delete Project'. The body says in one or two sentences what will happen and what is kept. Two Buttons sit in the Modal's `actions`: 'Cancel' first, a `<Button type="tertiary" size="small">`, then the action, a `<Button type="primary" size="small">` labelled in Title Case with the same verb as the title. When the action destroys or removes something, the action Button also has `color="danger"`. One case differs: 'Unsaved changes'. Its guard may have three Buttons, 'Cancel', "Don't Save" and 'Save', in that order. When it has two, its safe Button reads 'Keep Editing'. Escape and a click outside the Modal mean Cancel. While the request runs, the action Button is `loading` and keeps its label, and 'Cancel' is `state="disabled"`. The Modal stays open. It still calls `onClose` on Escape or a click outside, and the page ignores that call until the request ends. If the request fails, the Modal stays open and shows an inline error Alert at the top of its body, as the rule 'Form errors' says. When the action works, the Modal closes. If the thing is still on screen, the change shows where it is. If the thing is gone, a toast names it, as the rule 'Success feedback' says.
cases.why: A confirm is the last chance to stop a mistake. It has to say exactly what will happen, and the safe choice has to be easy to find.
do: Name the thing in the body: "This deletes 'Q3 plan' and its 12 tasks."
Say what is kept: 'Files in the repository are not changed.'
Give the title and the action the same verb, in Title Case: 'Delete Project' has a 'Delete' Button.
Disable 'Cancel' and ignore `onClose` while the request runs.
Close the Modal when the action works. Show the change where the thing is, or a toast that names it if the thing is gone.
dont: Do not label Cancel 'No' or 'Close'.
Do not label the action 'Yes, Delete', 'Confirm' or 'OK'.
Do not title the Modal 'Confirm Deletion' or 'Sure?'.
Do not change the action's label while it is loading, such as to 'Deleting…'.
Do not replace the Modal body with a spinner, or close the Modal, while the request runs.
Do not ask for a confirm when the action is easy to undo.
cases.native: On Apple use a system `confirmationDialog` or `.alert`, with the action in the `.destructive` role when it destroys or removes something. Never build a sheet by hand for a confirm.
cases.notBuiltYet: No Commentify confirm Modal uses `color="danger"`, and two of them label Cancel 'No'. Scindo on the web makes Cancel a secondary Button in some confirms and a tertiary one in others, and leaves its Delete Task and Remove Member confirms uncolored. Scindo on the web revokes an API key, and Commentify revokes an agent client, with no confirm.

cases.title: Create in a Modal
cases.situation: A person creates something new, such as a project or a task, and it needs a name before it exists.
do: Title the Modal 'Create' and the thing, such as 'Create Project', and give its action the same verb: 'Create'.
Put 'Cancel' first, a tertiary Button, then 'Create', a primary Button, in the Modal's `actions`.
Create on Enter too: put the fields in a `Form`.
Keep 'Create' `state="disabled"` while the name is empty.
Show `loading` on 'Create' while it runs, and keep the fields on screen with what the person typed.
Disable the fields while it runs, where the part allows it: the `TextField` and the `Checkbox`.
Focus the name field when the Modal opens, with `initialFocus="body"`.
Give a `RadioGroup` a line of text above it and an `aria-label` with the same words.
Show a name that is taken under the field, with `error` and `errorText`, and keep the Modal open.
Pick a safe default for every choice, so the person only has to type the name.
Close the Modal when it works and show the new thing where it lives.
dont: Do not replace the fields with a spinner while it creates.
Do not change the label while it is loading, such as to 'Creating…'.
Do not ask for more than the thing needs to exist. Everything else goes in its settings.
Do not show a toast when the new thing is on screen. It shows where it lives.
cases.native: On Apple use a sheet with a `Form`. Put 'Cancel' in the `.cancellationAction` placement and 'Create' in `.confirmationAction`, and create on `.onSubmit` from the name field.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web replaces the fields with a spinner while it creates a workspace or a task, and makes Cancel a secondary Button. Scindo's Apple app labels the Button 'Creating...' while it runs.

options.title: Just a name
options.useWhen: One name is enough. Everything else can be set later.

options.title: A name and a few choices
options.useWhen: The thing needs two or three choices up front, such as who can see it.

cases.title: Empty list
cases.situation: A list has loaded, and there is nothing in it yet.
do: Use `size="large"` when the list is the whole pane, and `size="small"` inside a section.
Say what is empty in the person's words: 'No archived projects'.
Say in `secondText` what will appear here: 'Projects you archive appear here.'
dont: Do not show a bare line of text, or nothing at all.
Do not use the system's words, such as 'No data' or 'No items found'.
Do not show the empty text while the list is still loading.
cases.native: On Apple use `ContentUnavailableView`, with the same words.
cases.notBuiltYet: Commentify writes most of its empty lists in Title Case, such as 'No Comments Available', and gives them no `secondText`.

options.title: Whole pane
options.useWhen: The list is the whole pane, such as a page of projects.

options.title: Inside a section
options.useWhen: The list sits inside a settings section or a card, next to other things.

cases.title: Empty lists
cases.situation: A list, table or pane has nothing to show.
cases.answer: Use `EmptyBox`, never a bare line of text. Its `size` is `large` when the list fills the whole region and `small` inside a section. The `text` says what is empty, in the person's words and in sentence case: 'No saved comments'. The `secondText` says what will appear here or what to do. When the person can fix it, pass the Button as `action`. An empty search shows the words searched for and a 'Clear Search' Button. A failed load is not an empty list: say that loading failed and offer a 'Try Again' Button. `EmptyBox` may hold that message, with 'Try Again' as its `action`, but never the empty text.
cases.why: An empty space looks like something is broken. Saying what is missing and what will fill it tells the person nothing is wrong and what to do next.
do: Say what is empty in the person's words: 'No saved comments'.
Say in `secondText` what will appear here or what to do: 'Comments you save appear here.'
Pass the Button that fills the list as `action`, such as 'Create Project'.
Show the words searched for and a 'Clear Search' Button when a search finds nothing.
Say that loading failed and offer a 'Try Again' Button when the list could not load.
dont: Do not show a bare line of text, or nothing at all, when a list is empty.
Do not show the empty text when the list failed to load.
Do not use the system's words, such as 'No data' or 'No records found'.
Do not pass an `action` the person is not allowed to use.
cases.native: On Apple use `ContentUnavailableView`, with the same words.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web uses `EmptyBox` in three places and bare text elsewhere, such as 'No API keys yet.' Commentify uses `EmptyBox` in most lists and bare text in a few. Commentify admin and jinhwankim.com show bare text. No product passes an `action` yet.

cases.title: Empty because it is not set up
cases.situation: A pane is empty because something it needs is not set up yet, such as a connected account.
do: Say what is missing: 'No calendar connected'.
Pass one Button as `action`, named for what it sets up: 'Connect Calendar'.
Say where the fix lives when it is not here: 'An admin can connect one in Settings, under Integrations.'
dont: Do not put the Button outside `EmptyBox`. Pass it as `action`.
Do not offer a Button the person is not allowed to use.
Do not offer more than one Button.
cases.native: On Apple use `ContentUnavailableView`, with the Button in its `actions`.
cases.notBuiltYet: Commentify puts its 'Open Settings' Button under `EmptyBox`, not in its `action`, and writes the text in Title Case: 'No App, Team, or User Connected'.

options.title: Fix it here
options.useWhen: The person can fix it here, with one Button.

options.title: Say where to fix it
options.useWhen: The fix lives somewhere else, or someone else has to do it. Say where in `secondText`.

cases.title: Empty search
cases.situation: A search or a filter finds nothing.
do: Use `icon="Search"`, so it reads as a search and not an empty list.
Show the words searched for: 'No results for "q3 plan"'.
Pass a 'Clear Search' Button as `action`. It empties the field and shows the whole list again.
Keep the words in the search field.
dont: Do not say 'No results found' without the words searched for.
Do not show the list's own empty text, such as 'No projects yet'.
Do not clear the search field unless the person asks.
cases.native: On Apple use `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)`.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web shows a bare line, 'No results found', with no words and no way to clear them. Scindo on Apple shows 'No results found' in a `ContentUnavailableView`, without the words. Commentify shows the words in an `EmptyBox`, with no Clear Search Button.

options.title: The words and a way to clear them
options.useWhen: A search or a filter finds nothing.

cases.title: Error page
cases.situation: Something broke while showing a page, and the app cannot show it.
do: Name the page in a `Heading` with `level={1}`: 'Something went wrong'.
Say in one plain sentence what happened and what the person can do.
Offer 'Try Again' first and 'Go Home' second.
Keep the navigation when only one route failed.
dont: Do not show the error's own message, a stack trace or an error id.
Do not show a line of text with no way out.
Do not hide the navigation when only one route failed.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web shows the error's own message and its id. Commentify shows one line and 'Try again', with no heading and no way home. jinhwankim.com shows an `EmptyBox` with no Button.

options.title: Full page
options.useWhen: The app shell itself failed, so nothing else can show.

options.title: Inside the shell
options.useWhen: One route failed and the navigation still works.

cases.title: Feedback form
cases.situation: A person sends feedback about the product from inside it.
do: Title the Modal 'Send Feedback' and label its action 'Send', after 'Cancel'.
Ask for a category with a `Select` and the feedback with a `Textarea`. Start the category on a safe default.
Put a line of text above the `Select` that says what it asks, and give the Select the same words as its `aria-label`.
Focus the first field when the Modal opens, with `initialFocus="body"`.
Disable the `Select` and the `Textarea` while it sends, and keep what the person wrote.
Keep 'Send' `state="disabled"` while the feedback is empty.
Send on Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter from the `Textarea`, through its `onSubmit`. Enter adds a new line.
Show an inline error Alert at the top of the Modal when sending fails, and keep what the person wrote.
Close the Modal when it works, and show a toast: 'Feedback sent.'
dont: Do not replace the form with a thank-you message that closes on its own.
Do not change the label while it is loading, such as to 'Sending...'.
Do not fail without a word. Say that the feedback was not sent.
Do not clear what the person wrote when sending fails.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo's feedback form labels the Button 'Sending...' while it runs, shows no error when sending fails, and replaces the form with a thank-you that closes after 1.5 seconds. It labels its fields with captions written by hand.

options.title: Send from a Modal
options.useWhen: Feedback can be sent from anywhere in the product, such as a help menu.

cases.title: Form errors
cases.situation: A form was submitted and something is wrong.
cases.answer: A problem with one field shows under that field, through the field's `error` and `errorText`. A problem with the whole request shows above the fields in `<Alert type="error" variant="inline" showCloseButton>`, so it stays until the person closes it or submits again. Its `onClose` clears the message; if it does not, the Alert comes back. While the request runs, the submit Button is `loading` and keeps its label. The form keeps what the person typed. The next submit clears the old messages. Messages are in sentence case. It is never a colored caption written by hand, and never the browser's `alert()`.
cases.why: A message next to the problem tells the person what to fix without searching for it. Keeping what they typed means they fix one thing instead of starting again.
do: Show a problem with one field under that field, with `error` and `errorText`.
Say what to do, not only what is wrong: 'Enter an email address, like name@acme.com.'
Show a problem with the whole request above the fields in `<Alert type="error" variant="inline" showCloseButton>`.
Clear the message in the Alert's `onClose`.
Keep everything the person typed after a failed submit.
Clear the old messages when the person submits again.
dont: Do not leave out `variant="inline"`: the default variant is a toast at the top of the screen, away from the form.
Do not write a red caption by hand. Use `errorText` or an Alert.
Do not use the browser's `alert()`.
Do not clear the form after a failed submit.
Do not change the submit Button's label while it is loading, such as to 'Saving…'.
cases.notBuiltYet: Commentify writes red captions by hand on its consent screen and in its Figma import dialog. Scindo on the web does the same in its dialogs, such as renaming a workspace or a task. Commentify uses the browser's `alert()` in three files, and Scindo on the web in one.

cases.title: Import from a checklist
cases.situation: A person picks which items to bring in from another place, such as pages from a wiki.
do: Put a search field at the top, then a count line, then the list of `Checkbox`es.
Write the count line as plain words: '3 of 8 pages selected'.
Offer 'Select All' and 'Clear' as tertiary Buttons. Both act on the items shown, and while a search is on their labels say so: 'Select All 2 Shown', 'Clear 2 Shown'.
Focus the search field when the Modal opens, with `initialFocus="body"`, and again after 'Clear Search'.
Count the selection in the action: 'Import 3 Pages'. Keep it `state="disabled"` while nothing is selected.
Keep the selection when a search hides items. Items that are filtered out stay selected.
Show `EmptyBox size="small"` with the words searched for and a 'Clear Search' Button when nothing matches.
Show `EmptyBox size="small"` when there is nothing left to import.
Show `loading` on the action while it imports, and keep the list on screen with the Checkboxes disabled.
Close the Modal when it works and show the new items where they live.
dont: Do not use a master Checkbox for Select All. Checkbox has no state for some selected.
Do not label the action 'Import' without the count, or change it while it runs, such as to 'Importing… 1/2'.
Do not clear the selection when the person searches.
Do not show a bare line of text when the list is empty or nothing matches.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo's Notion import labels its Buttons 'Select all' and 'Import', changes the action to 'Importing… 1/2' while it runs, and shows bare text when nothing matches.

options.title: Pick in a Modal
options.useWhen: The person chooses some items out of a list they can search.

cases.title: Form feedback
cases.situation: A person submits a small form, such as a settings field, and the request ends.
do: Show `loading` on the submit Button while the request runs, and keep its label.
Show 'Saved' on the Button for 2 seconds when the form saves in place, or until the person edits again.
Show a failed request above the fields in `<Alert type="error" variant="inline" showCloseButton>`, and keep what the person typed.
Call `toast({ type: 'success', message })` when the result is somewhere else.
dont: Do not change the Button's label while it is loading, such as to 'Saving…'.
Do not show a toast for a change the person can already see.
Do not let a failed save pass with no message.
Do not say 'successfully'.
cases.native: On Apple there is no toast. Show the result in place.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web labels its save Buttons 'Saving...' while they save. Its profile settings show nothing when a save fails. Its instructions settings show the error's own message in an inline Alert with no close button.

options.title: Saved on the Button
options.useWhen: The form saves in place, and the change shows where it is.

options.title: Inline error Alert
options.useWhen: The request failed.

options.title: Toast
options.useWhen: The result shows somewhere else, such as an invite that was sent.

cases.title: Invite a member
cases.situation: A person invites someone to join a workspace.
do: Title the Modal 'Invite Member' and label its action 'Send Invite', after 'Cancel'.
Send on Enter too: put the email field in a `Form`.
Focus the email field when the Modal opens, with `initialFocus="body"`, and disable it while the invite is sent.
Show a problem with the address under the field, such as a person who is already a member.
Close the Modal once the invite is sent, and show a toast that names the address: 'Invite sent to ada@example.com.'
Show the link in a `TextField` with `readOnly`, so it can be selected, and a 'Copy' Button next to it.
Change 'Copy' to 'Copied' for 2 seconds, and only when the link reached the clipboard.
Say under the field when copying is blocked: 'Copying is blocked here. Select the link and copy it.'
Say who can use the link and when it stops working.
List the links that still work, each with a 'Revoke' Button. Revoking removes access, so confirm it in the row, as the case 'Confirm a destructive action' does.
Give each row's 'Revoke', and the confirm's 'Cancel' and 'Revoke', an `aria-label` that names the link: 'Revoke the link made by Dana Lee'.
Disable 'Done', and ignore Escape and a click outside, while a revoke runs.
dont: Do not label the way out 'Close', or the action 'Create Invite' when the product sends it.
Do not replace the field with a spinner while the invite is sent.
Do not show 'Copied' when the copy failed, or 'Copied!' with an exclamation mark.
Do not revoke a link on the first click.
Do not touch `navigator` while the page renders. Copy only in the click handler.
cases.native: On Apple use a sheet with a `Form`, share the link with `ShareLink`, and revoke a link with a `.destructive` Button that asks first in a `confirmationDialog`.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web replaces the fields with a spinner while it creates an invite, labels the way out 'Close', reads 'Copied!', and cancels an invite link on one click with no confirm. Scindo's Apple app cancels a pending invite with no confirm too.

options.title: Send an invite by email
options.useWhen: The product sends the invite to an address the person types.

options.title: Share an invite link
options.useWhen: The person shares a link themselves, in their own chat or email.

cases.title: Load failure
cases.situation: A list or a section could not load.
do: Say what could not load: 'Could not load projects'.
Offer a 'Try Again' Button. It is `loading` while it loads, and keeps its label.
Show the list as soon as it loads.
Keep the rest of the page working when only one section failed.
Give the inline error Alert for a failed section no close button and `autoDismiss={false}`, so it stays until the section loads.
dont: Do not show the empty text, such as 'No projects yet', when the list failed to load.
Do not show the error's own message, such as 'Failed to fetch'.
Do not replace the whole page when only one section failed.
cases.native: On Apple use `ContentUnavailableView`, with a 'Try Again' Button in its `actions`.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web offers no Try Again when a list fails to load the first time. Commentify puts its 'Try again' Button under `EmptyBox`, not in its `action`.

options.title: Whole list failed
options.useWhen: The whole list failed to load, so there is nothing else to show in its place.

options.title: One section failed
options.useWhen: One section failed to load and the rest of the page works.

cases.title: Log out confirm
cases.situation: A person chooses Log Out.
do: Call it 'Log Out' everywhere: the menu item, the Modal title and the action Button. The way back in is 'Log In'.
Say in one sentence what logging out means on this device.
Leave the action Button in the plain primary color. Logging out destroys nothing.
Show `loading` on 'Log Out' while it runs, then show the logged-out page.
dont: Do not mix 'Sign Out' with 'Log In'. Use one word family: 'Log Out' and 'Log In'.
Do not give the action Button `color="danger"`.
Do not ask 'Are you sure you want to log out?'.
Do not show a toast after logging out. The logged-out page says it.
cases.native: On Apple use a system `confirmationDialog` titled 'Log Out', with a 'Log Out' Button and 'Cancel' in the `.cancel` role. Leave out the `.destructive` role: nothing is destroyed.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web says 'Log Out' but colors it as danger. Scindo on Apple says 'Sign Out' and puts it in the destructive role. Commentify and Commentify admin say 'Sign Out', title the Modal 'Confirm Sign Out', label the action 'Yes, Sign Out' and ask 'Are you sure you want to sign out?'.

options.title: Confirm in a Modal
options.useWhen: Any product with a Log Out action.

cases.title: Login page
cases.situation: A person who already has an account opens the product and is not signed in.
do: Show a problem with one field under that field.
Show a refused sign-in or a failed request in an inline Alert above the fields.
When there is a password, put a text-only 'Forgot password?' Button right under the submit Button.
Name the provider on its button: 'Continue with Google'.
While signing in, show the loading state on the submit Button and keep the form in place.
dont: Do not clear the email field after a failed attempt.
Do not show sign-up fields on the login page; link or tab to sign-up.
Do not replace the form with a spinner while signing in.
Do not say which of the email or the password was wrong.
cases.native: On Apple use `SignInWithAppleButton` for Apple, a grouped form for the fields, and system buttons.
cases.notBuiltYet: Commentify and Scindo on the web replace the form with a spinner while signing in. They do not use the Button's loading state yet.

options.title: Centered column
options.useWhen: The product has one way in, and most people sign in with email and a password.

options.title: Brand beside the form
options.useWhen: First-time visitors land here and need one line on what the product is.

options.title: Provider first
options.useWhen: Most people sign in with Google, GitHub or Apple; email is the fallback.

options.title: Email only
options.useWhen: An internal tool with no passwords: the person gets a sign-in link by email.

cases.title: Page not found
cases.situation: A person opens a link to a page that does not exist.
do: Say 'Page not found' in a `Heading` with `level={1}`.
Add one line on what may have happened: 'The link may be wrong, or the page was moved or removed.'
Offer one Button home: 'Go Home'.
dont: Do not make '404' the heading.
Do not show a line of text with no way home.
Do not blame the person for the link.
cases.notBuiltYet: Commentify's page not found is one line of bare text, 'Page not found.', with no way home. Scindo on the web shows '404' as its heading, then bare text and a text link home. jinhwankim.com has no heading: it puts '404:' at the start of its `EmptyBox` text and labels its Button 'Go to Home'.

options.title: Full page
options.useWhen: The address is outside the app shell, so nothing else can show.

options.title: Inside the shell
options.useWhen: The address is inside the app and the navigation still works.

cases.title: Rename
cases.situation: A person renames something, such as a project or a channel.
do: Title the Modal 'Rename' and the thing, such as 'Rename Project', and give its action the same verb: 'Rename'.
Keep 'Rename' `state="disabled"` while the name is empty or unchanged.
Save on Enter too: put the field in a `Form`.
Show a name that is taken under the field, with `error` and `errorText`, and keep the Modal open.
Focus the field with `autoFocus` when the name becomes a field in place.
Save on Enter and when the person leaves the field. Cancel on Escape, and when the name is empty.
dont: Do not label the Modal's action 'Save' or 'OK'.
Do not show a toast after a rename. The new name shows where the old one was.
Do not save an empty name.
Do not drop what the person typed when they leave the field.
cases.native: On Apple rename in place in a list with a `TextField` and `.onSubmit`. Use an `.alert` with a `TextField` when the name is not on screen.
cases.notBuiltYet: Commentify's two renames disagree on what leaving the field does: a project name cancels, a tag name saves. Scindo on the web labels its rename Modals' action 'Save', shows 'Saving...' while it runs, and writes a taken name as a red caption by hand.

options.title: Rename in a Modal
options.useWhen: Rename is opened from a menu or from far away from the name.

options.title: Rename in place
options.useWhen: The name is on screen, and it becomes a field.

cases.title: Page loading
cases.situation: A page or a pane is loading, and there is nothing to show yet.
do: Show the shell as soon as it can, and the spinner only where content is loading.
Center the spinner in the space that is loading.
Replace the spinner with the content as soon as it loads.
dont: Do not put text with the spinner, such as 'Loading…'.
Do not cover the navigation with a spinner when only one pane is loading.
Do not show the empty text while the list is still loading.
cases.native: On Apple use `ProgressView()` with no label, centered in the pane.

options.title: Full screen
options.useWhen: Nothing can show yet, not even the navigation.

options.title: In one pane
options.useWhen: The shell shows and one pane loads.

cases.title: Success feedback
cases.situation: Something the person did has worked.
cases.answer: The feedback depends on where the result shows. A Button that is `loading` keeps its label, and the spinner shows that it is working. Only success changes a label. When a form saves in place, its Button is `loading`, then reads 'Saved' for 2 seconds, then its own label again. There is no toast. When the result is somewhere else or gone, as when something is deleted, sent, moved or duplicated somewhere else, or a long job has finished, call `toast({ type: 'success', message: '…' })` with one short sentence in the past tense, in sentence case. It closes after 5 seconds. When something is copied to the clipboard, a Button reads 'Copied' for 2 seconds, and an IconButton swaps its icon to `Check` for 2 seconds. The message names the thing and does not say 'successfully'.
cases.why: Feedback belongs where the person is looking. A change they can see needs only a word on the Button, and a result they cannot see needs a short message that names it.
do: Show `loading` on the Button while a form saves, then 'Saved' for 2 seconds.
Write a toast as one short sentence in the past tense that names the thing: 'Invite sent to Dana.'
Show 'Copied' on a copy Button, or the `Check` icon on a copy IconButton, for 2 seconds.
Mount one `Toaster` near the app root, and show every toast with `toast()`.
dont: Do not say 'successfully'.
Do not change a Button's label while it is loading, such as to 'Saving…' or 'Deleting…'.
Do not show a toast for a change the person can already see.
Do not build a toast from `Alert`. Use `toast()`.
Do not make the person close a success message.
cases.native: On Apple there is no toast. Show the result in place.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo on the web has no toast. It shows success in five ways: a 'Saved' Button label, a green caption, an inline Alert, a thank-you that replaces a dialog and a 'Copied' label. The timed ones clear after 1.5, 2, 3 or 4 seconds. Commentify shows toasts through `Alert`, one at a time, and many of them say 'successfully'.

cases.title: Type to confirm
cases.situation: A person asks to delete something large that cannot be brought back, such as a workspace or an account.
do: Ask for typing only when the loss is permanent and large, such as a workspace with everything in it, or an account.
Ask for the thing's name when it has one. Ask for a fixed word, such as DELETE, when it does not.
Put the text to type in the field's label: 'Type Acme Design to confirm'.
Keep the action Button `state="disabled"` until the typed text matches exactly.
Match with case: 'acme design' does not match 'Acme Design'. Allow pasting the text.
Say above the field what is deleted and what is kept.
dont: Do not ask for typing for an everyday delete. A plain confirm is enough.
Do not block pasting into the field.
Do not change the action's label while it is loading, such as to 'Deleting…'.
Do not show a failed request as a red caption written by hand. Use an inline error Alert.
cases.native: On Apple use an `.alert` with a `TextField` in it. Put the action in the `.destructive` role and disable it until the text matches.
cases.notBuiltYet: Commentify matches its phrase with any case and ignores spaces around it, and labels its Button 'Deleting…' while it runs. Scindo labels its Button 'Deleting...' on the web and on Apple, and on the web its Delete Workspace Modal shows a failed request as a red caption written by hand.

options.title: Type the name in a Modal
options.useWhen: The thing has a name to type, such as a workspace.

options.title: Type a word in place
options.useWhen: A danger zone on a settings page: the field appears in place, under what it deletes.

cases.title: Unsaved changes
cases.situation: A person closes or leaves something they changed and did not save.
do: Ask only when there are changes. With nothing changed, close at once.
Title the Modal with the action it offers, such as 'Save Changes' or 'Discard Reply', and name the thing in the body.
Put 'Cancel' first, then 'Don't Save', then 'Save'. As in every confirm, the safe choice comes first and the main action last.
Make 'Cancel' tertiary, 'Don't Save' secondary and 'Save' primary, all `size="small"`.
Offer 'Keep Editing' and a danger 'Discard' when the product cannot save. 'Keep Editing' comes first.
Disable 'Cancel' and 'Don't Save' while 'Save' runs, and leave only when the save works.
dont: Do not ask when nothing changed.
Do not leave when the save fails. Keep the changes on screen.
Do not label the choices 'Yes' and 'No'.
Do not title the Modal 'Are you sure?'.
cases.native: On macOS a document window that closes with changes asks with the system alert: 'Save', 'Don't Save' and 'Cancel'. When the product cannot save, use a `confirmationDialog` with 'Discard' in the `.destructive` role and 'Keep Editing' in the `.cancel` role.
cases.notBuiltYet: No web product guards unsaved changes. Scindo on the web drops the changes to a document when the person chooses Cancel, with no question.

options.title: Save or discard
options.useWhen: The product can save the changes for the person, such as an edited document.

options.title: Discard or keep editing
options.useWhen: The product cannot save for the person, such as a reply that only posts when they say so.

cases.title: Upgrade prompt
cases.situation: A person reaches something their plan does not include, or a limit of their plan. When the agent is the one refused, follow the rule 'An agent refuses clearly' too.
do: Say what is locked and which plan unlocks it: 'Exporting to PDF is part of the Pro plan.'
Say which limit was reached, with the number, and when it resets: 'You have used all 50 agent replies for November.'
Offer 'Not Now' as a tertiary Button, then 'Upgrade to Pro' as a primary Button.
Show 'Upgrade to Pro' only to a person who can change the plan. Tell everyone else to ask a workspace admin, and give them only 'Not Now'.
Title the Modal 'Upgrade to Pro' only for a person who can upgrade. For everyone else, name what is locked: 'PDF Export Is on Pro'.
Follow the rule 'Confirm dialogs' for the Modal: `size="small"`, and Escape or a click outside means 'Not Now'.
Put the notice where the control was, with the same two Buttons, when a limit is reached inside a flow.
dont: Do not title the Modal 'Upgrade Required' or 'This is available on Pro plan only'. Name the action: 'Upgrade to Pro'.
Do not label the way out 'Maybe Later' or 'Close'.
Do not show an Upgrade Button to someone who cannot upgrade.
Do not hide the locked control. Let the person press it and learn what unlocks it.
Do not build the overlay by hand. Use `Modal`, which closes on Escape.
cases.native: On Apple show the notice in place, with an Upgrade Button only for admins. It opens the plan sheet in the app, never a link to a web page.
cases.notBuiltYet: Scindo's upgrade prompt on the web is an overlay built by hand that does not close on Escape, is titled 'Upgrade Required' and shows Upgrade to everyone. Commentify's upgrade Modal labels its Buttons 'Maybe Later' and 'Upgrade'.

options.title: Explain in a Modal
options.useWhen: The person pressed something their plan does not include.

options.title: Replace the control
options.useWhen: A limit was reached inside a flow. The notice takes the place of the control that hit it.
